newsitem.title: UK: Decorate emergency rooms nicely, Britain says.
newsitem.headline: Decorate emergency rooms nicely, Britain says.

text.p: Accident and Emergency units should be "attractively decorated" to reduce stress and the risk that patients or relatives may attack staff, Britain's National Health Service (NHS) said on Monday.
It recommended that soothing watercolours and landscapes be put on walls and that wards be decorated in colour schemes that have a positive effect on mood and do not clash.
"If the...unit is attractively decorated then it will have a calming influence," health minister Baroness Jay said in a statement.

"Careful selection of colour schemes is important as some colours can have an effect on the mood of the observer. Some have a calming effect -- green, bluish-green, yellowish-green -- while colours such as bright yellow and red can be a source of irritation."
The guidelines are meant in part to help counter a growing number of attacks on hospital and emergency staff.
Jay's office also recommends providing big, comfortable seats, televisions and interesting reading material.
"Building design and layout is very, very important indeed," said a spokeswoman for the NHS Trust Confederation, which represents hospital managers.
"Hospitals have to redecorate their premises from time to time. I think they will want to go ahead with these changes as quickly as possible."
